headline: Mergers loom. Funding flows. Delays persist.
deck: This week saw substantial acquisitions and funding rounds, alongside persistent delays in hypersonic testing.

stories.head: MDA Space spends $620 million on Blue Canyon
stories.body: MDA Space is acquiring Blue Canyon Technologies for $620 million, marking a strategic entry into the U.S. government market. This acquisition highlights the trend of foreign firms seeking local partners to navigate the complex U.S. defense landscape. It’s a classic case of 'if you can’t beat them, buy them.'
stories.soWhat: MDA’s move signals that the U.S. defense market is still an attractive playground, even for international players.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190 million for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in Series C funding, pushing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The company focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness, areas increasingly prioritized by the DoD. With this influx of cash, they’re poised to capitalize on government contracts that are becoming more lucrative.
stories.soWhat: It’s a clear indicator that investors are betting on the military’s growing appetite for space security solutions.

stories.head: Hypersonic glide-vehicle tests slip for third quarter
stories.body: Hypersonic glide-vehicle tests have been delayed for the third consecutive quarter, raising questions about the program’s viability. Northrop Grumman claims the industry is ready to scale solid rocket production, but the ongoing delays suggest a disconnect between ambition and execution. It feels less like a race and more like a leisurely stroll.
stories.soWhat: This trend could impact defense contracts, as the government may reconsider its commitments if progress continues to stall.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Blue Canyon's integration
watchlist.body: MDA's acquisition will likely lead to shifts in U.S. defense contracts, worth monitoring for potential impacts on competitors.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's next moves post-funding
watchlist.body: With the fresh capital, True Anomaly could pivot into new contracts or expand its technology offerings—watch for announcements.

watchlist.title: Northrop Grumman's production scaling efforts
watchlist.body: As they push for solid rocket production, any hiccups could ripple through the supply chain and affect timelines.

watchlist.title: ElevationSpace's Series B implications
watchlist.body: Their $40 million raise could signal a trend in funding for smaller players in the space sector, worth tracking.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
